32891-phantom-of-the-forest.title: Phantom Of The Forest
32891-phantom-of-the-forest.creator: Unknown
32891-phantom-of-the-forest.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. He tried to concentrate on the road once more. They had come six miles from Indian River. The road was just a white line, leading up and down long rows of dark evergreens. The snow filled the air, tangling his thoughts, filling the world with stinging, blinding particles of white. The snow actually seemed to hurt his eyes. It seemed to be hitting his eyeballs.

78632-a-bull-movement-in-yellow-horse.title: A Bull Movement In Yellow Horse
78632-a-bull-movement-in-yellow-horse.creator: Unknown
78632-a-bull-movement-in-yellow-horse.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. “Aw, come on, Slim, let’s find out what she is anyway. All this time she’s gittin’ further and further away. Mebby she’s uh harmless beast and we can haze her into Yaller Hoss and have some fun. I’d shore like to show that alleged bad man’s town something new. Let’s hit th’ old highwater trail, Slim.

9219-edward-fane-s-rosebud-from-twice-to.title: Edward Fane S Rosebud From Twice Told Tales
9219-edward-fane-s-rosebud-from-twice-to.creator: Unknown
9219-edward-fane-s-rosebud-from-twice-to.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. wn upward, gathering thriftily into her person the whole warmth of the fire, which, now at nightfall, begins to dissipate the autumnal chill of her chamber. The blaze quivers capriciously in front, alternately glimmering into the deepest chasms of her wrinkled visage, and then permitting a ghostly dimness to mar the outlines of her venerable figure.

arxiv-2108-13769.title: Implementation of hitting times of discrete time quantum random walks on Cubelike graphs.
arxiv-2108-13769.creator: Jaideep Mulherkar, Rishikant Rajdeepak, V Sunitha
arxiv-2108-13769.description: Abstract . We demonstrate an implementation of the hitting time of a discrete time quantum random walk on cubelike graphs using IBM’s Qiskit platform. Our implementation is based on efficient circuits for the Grover and Shift operators. We verify the results about the one-shot hitting time of quantum walks on a hypercube as proved in [ Kempe2005 ] .

arxiv-2110-05242.title: Accelerating Multi-Objective Neural Architecture Search by Random-Weight Evaluation
arxiv-2110-05242.creator: Shengran Hu, Ran Cheng ∗, Cheng He, Zhichao Lu, Jing Wang, Miao Zhang
arxiv-2110-05242.description: Abstract For the goal of automated design of high-performance deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Neural Architecture Search (NAS) methodology is becoming increasingly important for both academia and industries. Due to the costly stochastic gradient descent (SGD) training of CNNs for performance evaluation, most existing NAS methods are computationally expensive for real-world deployments.

arxiv-2211-04755.title: Towards Global Crop Maps with Transfer Learning
arxiv-2211-04755.creator: Hyun-Woo Jo, Alkiviadis Koukos, Vasileios Sitokonstantinou, Woo-Kyun Lee Charalampos Kontoes
arxiv-2211-04755.description: Abstract The continuous increase in global population and the impact of climate change on crop production are expected to affect the food sector significantly. In this context, there is need for timely, large-scale and precise mapping of crops for evidence-based decision making.

arxiv-2302-06873.title: Lero : A Learning-to-Rank Query Optimizer
arxiv-2302-06873.creator: Rong Zhu # , Wei Chen #, Bolin Ding, Xingguang Chen, Andreas Pfadler, Ziniu Wu, Jingren Zhou ∗
arxiv-2302-06873.description: Abstract . A recent line of works apply machine learning techniques to assist or rebuild cost-based query optimizers in DBMS. While exhibiting superiority in some benchmarks, their deficiencies, e.g., unstable performance, high training cost, and slow model updating, stem from the inherent hardness of predicting the cost or latency of execution plans using machine learning models.

arxiv-2302-08967.title: sMRI-PatchNet: A novel explainable patch-based deep learning network for Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis and discriminative atrophy localisation with Structural MRI
arxiv-2302-08967.creator: Xin Zhang, Liangxiu Han*, Lianghao Han, Haoming Chen, Darren Dancey, Daoqiang Zhang
arxiv-2302-08967.description: Abstract Structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) can identify subtle brain changes due to its high contrast for soft tissues and high spatial resolution. It has been widely used in diagnosing neurological brain diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the size of 3D high-resolution data poses a significant challenge for data analysis and processing.

arxiv-2303-14875.title: Regularity of pullback attractors for nonclassical diffusion equations with delay
arxiv-2303-14875.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . In this paper, we mainly study the regularity of pullback 𝒟 \mathcal{D} -attractors for a nonautonomous nonclassical diffusion equation with delay term b ⁡ ( t , u t ) b(t,u_{t}) which contains some hereditary characteristics.

arxiv-2411-00201.title: YOLO Evolution: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Architectural Review of YOLOv12, YOLO11, and Their Previous Versions
arxiv-2411-00201.creator: Nidhal Jegham, Chan Young Koh, Marwan Abdelatti, Abdeltawab Hendawi
arxiv-2411-00201.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nidhal Jegham, Chan Young Koh, Marwan Abdelatti, Abdeltawab Hendawi. This study presents a comprehensive benchmark analysis of various YOLO (You Only Look Once) algorithms. It represents the first comprehensive experimental evaluation of YOLOv3 to the latest version, YOLOv12, on various object detection challenges. The challenges considered include varying object sizes, diverse aspect ratios, and small-sized objects of a single class, ensuring a comprehensive assessment across datasets with distinct challenges.

arxiv-2501-10167.title: Improved phase field model for two-phase incompressible flows: Sharp interface limit, universal mobility and surface tension calculation
arxiv-2501-10167.creator: Jing-Wei Chen, Chun-Yu Zhang, Hao-Ran Liu, Hang Ding
arxiv-2501-10167.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose an improved phase field model for interface capturing in simulating two-phase incompressible flows. The model incorporates a second-order diffusion term, which utilizes a nonlinear coefficient to assess the degree of deviation of interface profile from its equilibrium state.

arxiv-2503-03532.title: AI-Enabled Conversational Journaling for Advancing Parkinson’s Disease Symptom Tracking
arxiv-2503-03532.creator: Mashrur Rashik, Shilpa Sweth, Nishtha Agrawal, Saiyyam Kochar, Kara M Smith, Fateme Rajabiyazdi, Vidya Setlur, Narges Mahyar, Ali Sarvghad
arxiv-2503-03532.description: Abstract . Journaling plays a crucial role in managing chronic conditions by allowing patients to document symptoms and medication intake, providing essential data for long-term care. While valuable, traditional journaling methods often rely on static, self-directed entries, lacking interactive feedback and real-time guidance. This gap can result in incomplete or imprecise information, limiting its usefulness for effective treatment.

arxiv-2506-17028.title: Optimal Sobolev inequalities of high order with L 2 − L^{2}- remainder
arxiv-2506-17028.creator: Lorenzo Carletti, Frédéric Robert
arxiv-2506-17028.description: Abstract . We investigate the validity of the optimal higher-order Sobolev inequality H k 2 ​ ( M n ) ↪ L 2 ​ n n − 2 ​ k ​ ( M n ) H_{k}^{2}(M^{n})\hookrightarrow L^{\frac{2n}{n-2k}}(M^{n}) on a closed Riemannian manifold when the remainder term is the L 2 − L^{2}- norm.

arxiv-2507-21459.title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: DR6 Sunyaev-Zel’dovich Selected Galaxy Clusters Catalog
arxiv-2507-21459.creator: ACT/DES/HSC Collaboration: M. Aguena 1,2, S. Aiola 3,4, S. Allam 5, F. Andrade-Oliveira 6, D. Bacon 7, N. Bahcall 8, N. Battaglia 9, E. S. Battistelli 10, S. Bocquet 11, B. Bolliet 12,13, J. R. Bond 14, D. Brooks 15, E. Calabrese 16, J. Carretero 17, S. K. Choi 18, L. N. da Costa 2, M. Costanzi 19,1
arxiv-2507-21459.description: Abstract We present the results of a search for galaxy clusters in the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) Data Release 6 (DR6) microwave sky maps covering 16293 square degrees in three frequency bands, using data obtained over the lifetime of the project (2008–2022).

arxiv-2507-22151.title: Efficient detection of localization transitions using predictability
arxiv-2507-22151.creator: Tiago Pernambuco, Jonas Maziero, Rafael Chaves
arxiv-2507-22151.description: Abstract Identifying phase transition points is a fundamental challenge in condensed matter physics, particularly for transitions driven by quantum interference effects, such as Anderson and many-body localization. Recent studies have demonstrated that quantum coherence provides an effective means of detecting localization transitions, offering a practical alternative to full quantum state tomography and related approaches.

arxiv-2511-22738.title: Rigidity of the unstable foliation
arxiv-2511-22738.creator: Sergi Burniol Clotet
arxiv-2511-22738.description: Abstract We establish a rigidity result for the unstable foliations of transitive Anosov flows on 3-manifolds: if the unstable foliations of two such flows are equivalent (that is, if there exists a homeomorphism mapping one foliation to the other), then the flows are topologically conjugate up to a constant change of time.

arxiv-2512-02692.title: Nucleon decays into three leptons: noncontact contributions
arxiv-2512-02692.creator: Jing Chen, Yi Liao, Xiao-Dong Ma, Hao-Lin Wang
arxiv-2512-02692.description: Abstract We investigate baryon number violating (BNV) nucleon decays into three leptons from noncontact contributions that are induced by dimension-6 (dim-6) BNV operators in low-energy effective field theory (LEFT) with an exchange of a baryon, meson, lepton, or photon field.

arxiv-2604-02535.title: A Spectral Framework for Multi-Scale Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction
arxiv-2604-02535.creator: \authororcid Zeyang Huang0000-0003-3945-1274, \authororcid Angelos Chatzimparmpas0000-0002-9079-2376, \authororcid Thomas Höllt0000-0001-8125-1650, and \authororcid Takanori Fujiwara0000-0002-6382-2752

pmc-10539958.title: First report of frequencies of Y chromosome microdeletions at a reproductive medicine center in Peru
pmc-10539958.creator: M Gavilan, C Vivar, V Núñez, C Choque, M Guzmán, C Duarte
pmc-10539958.description: ObjectiveY chromosome Microdeletions are the second genetic cause of infertility in men. Despite its importance for infertility treatment, there is no previous research in Peru. The aim of this study was to determine the frequencies and characteristics of Y chromosome microdeletions in a group of men who sought infertility consultation at a specialized reproductive medicine center in Peru.

pmc-10595192.title: Genus-Wide Transcriptional Landscapes Reveal Correlated Gene Networks Underlying Microevolutionary Divergence in Diatoms
pmc-10595192.creator: Nathan G Walworth, Josh L Espinoza, Phoebe A Argyle, Jana Hinners, Naomi M Levine, Martina A Doblin, Chris L Dupont, Sinéad Collins, Emily Josephs
pmc-10595192.description: Marine microbes like diatoms make up the base of marine food webs and drive global nutrient cycles. Despite their key roles in ecology, biogeochemistry, and biotechnology, we have limited empirical data on how forces other than adaptation may drive diatom diversification, especially in the absence of environmental change.

pmc-11516754.title: Social inequalities in cancer incidence, survival and mortality: An umbrella review
pmc-11516754.creator: M Francis, S Peña, T von Wright, E Lindell, I Bellos, V Benetou, L Kestilä
pmc-11516754.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundAn increasing number of systematic reviews investigating differences in cancer burden by social factors such as race, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status have been published in recent years. Our study aims to evaluate the strength and quality of evidence from systematic reviews investigating associations between social factors and cancer incidence, survival, and mortality to help policy-makers reduce existing social inequalities in the burden of cancer.MethodsOur study is a pre-registered umbrella review (PROSPERO; CRD42024552884).

pmc-12567223.title: Glucagon in Pediatric Metabolic Disorders: Pathophysiology and Therapeutic Perspectives
pmc-12567223.creator: Giada Di Pietro, Francesco Chiarelli, Angelika Mohn
pmc-12567223.description: Over the past century of research, it has become increasingly evident that glucagon should no longer be regarded solely as a counter-regulatory hormone to insulin. Its role in the pathophysiology of metabolic disorders—including diabetes, obesity, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease—appears to be critical.

pmc-12728000.title: Real-world patient outcomes with Blinatumomab and Inotuzumab in adult relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia: a retrospective analysis from two Romanian oncology centers
pmc-12728000.creator: Ion Antohe, Amalia Titieanu, Vlad Andrei Cianga, Cosmin Minciună, Cătălin Dănăilă, Alina Daniela Tănase, Iuliu Ivanov, Loredana Dragoş, Mihaela Zlei, Mihaela Mențel, Ciprian Tomuleasa, Anamaria Bancos, Manuela Ciocoiu, Angela Dăscălescu
pmc-12728000.description: IntroductionThe management of adult relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (R/R B-ALL) remains a significant challenge, with patients presenting particularly poor historical outcomes. Novel immunotherapies, such as Blinatumomab and Inotuzumab, have revived the therapeutic landscape of R/R B-ALL, but their optimal sequencing, toxicity management, and post-transplant integration remain unclear, particularly in real-world, resource-limited settings.

pmc-13032902.title: Influence of mycorrhizae and silicon on maize and soybean resistance and tolerance to Spodoptera frugiperda (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)
pmc-13032902.creator: Lucas Adjuto Ulhoa, Arlindo Leal Boiça Júnior, Jeffrey A Davis, Michael Joseph Stout, Rachid Hanna
pmc-13032902.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Productivity of soybean, Glycine max (L.) Merr. (Fabales: Fabaceae), and maize, Zea mays L. (Poales: Poaceae), is reduced by several insect pests, among the most important of which is the fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda (J.E. Smith) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae). Control of this insect relies mainly on chemical insecticides or transgenic plants expressing Bacillus thuringiensis Berliner (Eubacteriales: Bacillaceae) proteins, but these methods impose strong selection pressure favoring resistance evolution.

pmc-13125893.title: Distal nerve transfers for ulnar nerve reinnervation and hand function restoration
pmc-13125893.creator: Andrija Savić, Jovan Grujić, Aleksandar Djurdjević, Svetozar Stanković, Aleksa Mićić, Aleksandra Stojiljković, Branko Gaković, Milan Lepić, Nenad Novaković, Lukas Rasulić
pmc-13125893.description: IntroductionUlnar nerve injuries lead to severe intrinsic hand muscle dysfunction and major impairment of grip, pinch, and quality of life. Distal nerve transfers have been introduced to overcome the limitations of conventional repair and grafting by shortening the regeneration distance and improving reinnervation of intrinsic muscles.

pmc-13316457.title: Plant Functional Groups Mediated the Effects of Plateau Pika Disturbance and Mowing on the Community Stability of Alpine Meadow Plants
pmc-13316457.creator: Yu Chai, Chengyi Li, Xinru Du, Xilai Li
pmc-13316457.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The composition of plant functional groups is a primary factor influencing grassland ecosystem stability. Currently, it remains unclear how plant functional groups mediate the effects of external disturbances on the stability of alpine meadow ecosystems. This study aims to fill this knowledge gap via a six‐year controlled experiment involving three levels of mowing intensity (unmown, moderate, and heavy) and three levels of plateau pika ( Ochotona curzoniae ) density (0, 93.3, and 186.7 individuals·ha−1).

pmc-13503800.title: Development and validation of the Life after Stroke questionnaire as a patient-reported outcome measure for stroke survivors living at home
pmc-13503800.creator: Wolfgang Brunner, Christoph Zenzmaier, Nina Huber, Julian Granna, Kurt Mölgg, Benjamin Dejakum, Silvia Felicetti, Anel Karisik, Stefan Kiechl, Christian Boehme, Michael Knoflach

pmc-13520511.title: μPADs for a Safer Night’s Sleep: An Alternative for Quality Control of Melatonin Pharmaceutical Formulations
pmc-13520511.creator: Ana Julia Aparecida Ramos, Laís Canniatti Brazaca, Eduardo Luiz Rossini, Manoel de Jesus de Aquino Lima, Emanuel Carrilho
pmc-13520511.description: Melatonin, known as the “sleep hormone,” has its primary function in regulating the circadian cycle, a 24 h sleep–wake pattern that leads to significant physical, mental, and behavioral changes. The use of melatonin in pharmaceutical formulations gained popularity as a tool to combat sleep disorders such as insomnia and has been increasing in the last few decades.

pmc-13561853.title: The Haematological and Biochemical Responses of Goat Bucks to Range Grazing and Indoor Concentrate‐Based Feeding Systems
pmc-13561853.creator: Selamu Abraham, Yisehak Kechero, Jane Wamatu
pmc-13561853.description: BackgroundRange grazing remains the principal feed resource for goats in smallholder production systems, particularly in regions where range grazing and intensive concentrate‐based systems coexist. However, expanding cropland has reduced the availability of grazing lands and shifted production toward concentrate‐based feeding systems.

pmc-13664734.title: In Vitro Modulatory Effect of Stimulant Beverages on the Growth Kinetics of Intestinal Bacteria Associated with Colorectal Cancer
pmc-13664734.creator: Tomas Kudera, Diana Karina Baigts-Allende, Barbora Fiserova, Ladislav Kokoska
pmc-13664734.description: Colorectal cancer is increasingly linked to diet-induced gut microbiota modulations, whereas the role of oncogenic bacteria is discussed. This study investigated the in vitro growth-modulatory effects of hot-water extracts of six stimulant beverages, namely Aspalathus linearis (rooibos), Coffea arabica, Coffea canephora (coffee), Camellia sinensis var. assamica, C. sinensis var.

uslaw-usc-t16-s395.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s395.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 1 (National Parks, Military Parks, Monuments, And Seashores); Subchapter XLI (Hawaii National Park). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Sole and exclusive jurisdiction shall be exercised by the United States over the territory which is now or may hereafter be included in the Hawaii National Park in the Territory of Hawaii, saving, however, to the Territory.
